queries.text: Nietzsche, Thus Spoke Zarathustra, “Of Old and Young Women,” translated from the author’s Portuguese. Public-domain English translation: Thomas Common. "para o prazer do guerreiro" rendered "for the recreation of the warrior" (as in the standard English versions); literal alternative: "for the warrior’s pleasure". "sempre amarga" (literally "always bitter") rendered "still bitter".
Lévi, Dogma and Ritual of High Magic, translated from the author’s Portuguese (which uses the archaic "tu", hence "thee/thy"). Compare Waite’s public-domain "Transcendental Magic" (1896).
The note is attached to "although that also counts" (physical strength). Read as: physical strength also counts, but in the sense of harming the relationship and making it worse. Kept literal.
Brazilian slang "banana" (a spineless, submissive man) rendered as "wimp". Alternatives: "pushover", "doormat" (used just below for "capachos").

The note opposes "domínio" (consented mastery/dominance) to "dominação" (coercive domination). Rendered "mastery" vs. "domination" here; elsewhere "domínio" is rendered "dominance" (e.g., note 18). "Domine-a" in the text is rendered "Take command of her" to match. Decide whether to unify "domínio" as "mastery" or "dominance" throughout.
